subject: parasitoid wasp
title: A Wasp Smaller Than a Rice Grain Lays Eggs in Ants in 0.05 Seconds

scenes.text: This wasp hunts ants that could tear it apart.
It's two millimetres long. Its targets are fast desert ants in Spain that fight back with jaws and legs.
So it never attacks head-on. It hovers behind a worker ant, waiting.
The moment the ant pauses, the wasp drops, grabs on and stabs an egg into its belly.
Grab, inject, fly away. The whole attack takes about a twentieth of a second.
Too fast to fight. The ant walks home with a wasp growing inside it.

description:
A wasp about two millimetres long lays its eggs inside desert ants that fight back with jaws and legs.
High-speed filming in Spain showed Kollasmosoma sentum attacks from behind when the ant pauses, and the whole grab-and-inject takes about 0.05 seconds on average.
Could you react in a twentieth of a second?
first_comment: The wasp was only discovered and named in 2011, after a researcher filmed it at ant nests near Madrid. What's the fastest thing you've ever seen an insect do?
